Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going? is a large painting by Paul Gauguin, made in Tahiti in 1897. It shows Tahitian figures from birth to old age in a dreamlike landscape.

Gauguin had come to Tahiti in 1891 looking for a world untouched by Europe, but found a French colony and a Christian kingdom already gone. He painted the Tahiti he imagined.

His paintings fixed the Western image of Polynesia, and of Polynesian women, for a century. Tahitians today view that image with mixed feelings, much as they view Typee. The picture hangs in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. See also modern art.
